methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one assumption ID (native_all_columns, owned_erasure, compiler, precision_tape, analytic_recovery), one quantified implication and exact dependency closure. Check current handoffs, including #5625 row reentry and #5707 root-prefix lowering, without treating their partial scope as the whole theorem. Prove or falsify that implication with a caller-bound argument; stop at the chosen obligation. Finite tests or root digits do not discharge an all-size statement.

actual_scope: Classify exactly when every aligned window of a dyadic instance (N = S+e and L powers of two, starts divisible by L) of the capped Gaussian source has longest selected run above 6W, under S >= e(6W+1); answer whether the uniform length condition L >= 12W+2 of research/core-production-nonempty can be sharpened on dyadic sections.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether one of the five inherited assumptions can be proved at its actual caller. This package settles one source-geometry question left open by PR6972 (dyadic aligned sections of its guard). It discharges no inherited assumption and proves nothing about the numerical, compiler or native obligations.
bottleneck_link: Side result on source geometry for analytic_recovery and compiler: PR6972 needs the source partition at every original complete context. This decides exactly which dyadic aligned sections have a nonempty interior and which are empty, for the length half of its guard.
stop_rule: Stop after the exact classification, the sharpness theorem and one exhaustive finite check; do not extend to non-dyadic periods or to S/e below 6W+1.
evidence: research/dyadic-aligned-window-guard/verify.py prints PASS_DYADIC_ALIGNED_WINDOW_GUARD; PROOF.md gives Theorems 1 to 3.

open_questions.question: Which aligned windows fail in dyadic instances with floor(S/e) <= 6W?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the S/e half of the guard in PR6972; its one-unit adverse family never occurs dyadically (N would be odd), and the next case S = e(6W+1)-2 is untouched here.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the hole-offset method with internal cells of length 6W or 6W+1 and test which aligned windows contain no (6W+1)-cell.
open_questions.blocked_by: The positions of the (6W+1)-cells form a Sturmian pattern; their offsets modulo L need a separate argument.

open_questions.question: What replaces the periodicity lemma when N is not a power of two but L divides N?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The Core's actual periods need not be powers of two; the classification then no longer applies as stated.
open_questions.first_step: For N = 2^a b with b odd, test whether the holes repeat with period N/2^j times a factor of b.
open_questions.blocked_by: L | N no longer forces the hole offsets modulo L to depend only on the odd part of e and on L.

open_questions.question: Can the classification of empty short aligned sections be used for the zero-dimensional branch of PR6972's open question 3?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It names exactly which aligned short sections are genuinely empty.
open_questions.first_step: Take one bad aligned section from verify.py (for example W = 1, L = 8, e = 8, N = 64) and trace it through the source, numerical, ownership and cost contracts.
open_questions.blocked_by: No native empty-interior service is supplied by either package.
